clue.text: Australian state initially provided for orphaned child

parts.note: Western Australia is shortened to its initials, WA
provided, as in 'on condition that', means if

explanation.surface: A child whose parents have died is being looked after by an Australian state government.
explanation.definitionFit: A waif is a homeless, neglected child, often one with no parents.

clue.text: Watch close to Inuit agitated polar bears

indicators.note: bears in the sense of carries within it, so the shuffled letters hold the other piece
agitated means stirred up, so the letters of polar are rearranged
close to means the final letter of the word Inuit

explanation.surface: Polar bears grow restless when an Inuit hunter comes near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges POLAR into PAROL, and 'bears' holds the T from 'close to Inuit' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch, as a noun, is a guard or lookout, and a patrol does the same job of keeping guard.

clue.text: Note parent admits also supporting more cycling

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a parent is a mother, informally mum

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed beneath, so the word for also comes after
cycling means the letters of more go round, the last letter moving to the front

parts.note: also means and

explanation.surface: A note in which a parent concedes they back more bike riding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' suggests bicycles but moves the last letter of 'more' to the front; in a down entry 'supporting' means sitting underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorandum is a written note, especially a short message within an office.

clue.text: Distinguished bowler briefly is worn by very old composer

indicators.note: a hat is worn by a person, so the abbreviations sit inside the bowler
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Sir Francis Drake, the Elizabethan seaman, famously finished his game of bowls before facing the Armada

explanation.surface: A smart bowler hat is worn by an ancient composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests a hat or cricketer; here it is Francis Drake, said to have played bowls as the Armada approached. 'briefly' cuts DRAKE to DRAK; 'is worn by' puts VO inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonin Dvorak was the Czech composer of the New World Symphony.

clue.text: Fashion-obsessed Ivor parading somewhat revolutionary outfits

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A style-conscious man called Ivor shows off clothes that are rather radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes SEDIVORP from 'Fashion-obsessed Ivor parading', and 'revolutionary' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To outfit someone is to equip or supply them, which is what provides means as a verb.

clue.text: Point of banquet without starter?

indicators.note: without starter means the first letter of the word for banquet is removed

parts.note: a banquet is a feast

explanation.surface: What is the point of a grand dinner that has no first course?
explanation.walkthrough: 'without starter' drops the F from FEAST. 'Starter' reads as a first course but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: Religious follower elected to quit order

indicators.note: to quit means to leave, so the letters for elected come out of the word for order

parts.note: order, as in good behaviour under control, is discipline
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: A member of a religious order chooses to leave it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to quit' takes IN out of DISCIPLINE; 'order' reads as a monastic order but means discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower of a religious teacher, as the twelve were of Jesus.

clue.text: Mint coin, sovereign maybe

parts.note: a penny is a coin
a sovereign, a monarch, is royal; the maybe marks it as one example of a royal person

explanation.surface: A newly minted coin, perhaps a gold sovereign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' and 'sovereign' read as coinage; Mint is the herb and a sovereign is a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Pennyroyal is a species of plant in the mint family, used in herbal remedies.

clue.text: Saw Bill cycle

parts.note: a bill is an advertisement, AD for short
a cycle is an age, a long period of time

explanation.surface: Bill rode his bike and saw something.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or proverb, the same as an adage.

clue.text: Reveal it's tricky adapting to different tasks

indicators.note: tricky suggests something intricate and deceptive, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Revealing that the job is difficult when switching between jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges the letters of REVEAL IT'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Versatile describes someone able to turn their hand to many different jobs.

clue.text: Extra from EastEnders broadcast creates excitement

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken aloud, and EastEnders are Cockneys, who say a th sound as v

parts.note: extra means further, as in further supplies

explanation.surface: An extra from the TV soap EastEnders makes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in the East End of London; Cockney speech turns further into 'furver', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervour is intense passion or enthusiasm, a strong form of excitement.

clue.text: Papal authority in Cavan, it disintegrated

indicators.note: disintegrated means broke into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Church authority in the Irish county of Cavan fell apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disintegrated' rearranges CAVAN IT; Cavan is a county in the Republic of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican is the seat of the Pope and stands for papal government.

clue.text: Upset, unfortunately, about Strictly's opening dance

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed word wraps the single letter
upset means turned over, so the word for unfortunately is read backwards

parts.note: alas is an expression meaning unfortunately

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word Strictly's

explanation.surface: A distressed viewer complains about the first dance on Strictly Come Dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns ALAS into SALA, and 'about' wraps it round the S from 'Strictly's opening'. Strictly Come Dancing is a BBC ballroom contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American dance, one of the styles on the show.

clue.text: Puts down two vessels, worried over breakages ultimately

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the last piece goes underneath

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, one vessel, and a jug is a second, for liquid
worried means ate, as in what's eating you

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of the word breakages

explanation.surface: Someone sets down a pair of jugs, anxious that they might get broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places ATE above the S at the foot of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To put down a rebellion or people is to crush them, which is to subjugate them.

clue.text: Forensic evidence found in lodging-house, according to criminal

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so the evidence goes into the lodging-house

parts.note: a kip is an old slang word for a cheap lodging-house
DNA is genetic evidence used in forensic science
per means according to, as in per the rules

explanation.surface: Police detectives turn up genetic traces in a boarding house, it is said, implicating a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidnapper is a criminal who abducts people and holds them for ransom.

clue.text: Oddly cheap current furniture keeps being satisfactory

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the odd letters sit within the other pieces

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a table is a piece of furniture

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third and fifth letters of the word cheap

explanation.surface: Cheap furniture for today is still good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' reads as 'strangely' but picks the odd-numbered letters of 'cheap'; 'current' is electrical, not 'modern'.
explanation.definitionFit: Acceptable means good enough to be accepted, which is to say adequate.

clue.text: Where account may be kept of politician's election slogan?

definitions.meaning: a British savings and mortgage institution where people hold accounts
read as words, ... could be a candidate's campaign promise to construct a better community

explanation.surface: An account of a politician's campaign slogan, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: A building society is a British mutual savings bank; the second reading takes the words literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Building societies are mutual institutions that keep savings accounts and lend money for houses.

clue.text: Business Republican will visit within Springfield, perhaps

parts.note: within means in

indicators.note: will visit means will go inside, so the letter enters the other pieces

parts.note: Dusty Springfield was a British singer, so Springfield is an example of a Dusty

explanation.surface: A Republican politician will call on a firm in Springfield, a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Springfield' reads as a town but is the singer Dusty Springfield. 'will visit' puts R into INDUSTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry means trade and commerce, a sector of business activity.

clue.text: Denial of eating nuts individual left unfinished

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of eating are mixed up
left unfinished means the last letter of the word for individual is cut off

parts.note: an individual is one

explanation.surface: Someone denies having eaten nuts, a single one left half eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' rearranges EATING into NEGATI; 'left unfinished' cuts ONE to ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Negation is the act of denying or contradicting something, a denial.

clue.text: Sound of a French mother, advanced in years

parts.note: un is French for a
a dam is an animal's mother
aged means old, advanced in years

explanation.surface: A noise made by a French mother who is elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noise but means healthy or intact.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound in the sense of whole and in good condition means undamaged.

clue.text: Vacuous types, say, with papers to take up and absorb

indicators.note: in a down clue, to take up means to lift, so the pieces read from the bottom upward
vacuous means empty, so only the outer letters of types remain

parts.note: say means for example, EG
papers, as in identity papers, is ID

explanation.surface: Empty-headed people, for example, take up papers and soak up what they read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacuous' empties TYPES to TS; 'to take up' reverses TS EG ID.
explanation.definitionFit: To digest information is to take it in and understand it fully.

clue.text: Fruit left behind is something highly prized

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the letter for left follows the fruit

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit that was left behind turns out to be very valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a precious gem, and figuratively anything of great value.

clue.text: Lively deliveries essentially following start of play

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the middle letters come after the start of a play

parts.note: a play starts with Act I, its first act

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so the middle letters of deliveries are taken

explanation.surface: A cricket match springs to life with bowling as soon as play starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts VE after ACT I, the first act of a play. 'deliveries' and 'play' suggest cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Active and lively both describe someone energetic and on the move.

clue.text: Attack in Tulsa dispersed by retired South American

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side
retired means withdrawn, so the abbreviation is read backwards
dispersed means scattered, so the letters of Tulsa are rearranged

explanation.surface: An assault in the Oklahoma city of Tulsa is broken up by a South American pensioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns SA into AS; 'dispersed' rearranges TULSA into SAULT.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent physical attack on someone.

clue.text: Encourage doctor to discharge child

indicators.note: to discharge means to let go, so the letters for child are released from the doctor

parts.note: a surgeon is a doctor
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Persuading a doctor to send a young patient home from hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to discharge' takes SON out of SURGEON.
explanation.definitionFit: To urge someone is to press or spur them on, to encourage them.

clue.text: Admittedly worked hard having change of heart

indicators.note: change of heart means the central letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: grafted is British slang for worked hard

explanation.surface: I admit I worked hard before changing my mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having change of heart' swaps the middle F of GRAFTED for N; graft is British slang for hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Granted, as a sentence adverb, concedes a point, meaning I admit.

clue.text: Textile worker said to be dreadful

indicators.note: said means spoken aloud, so the word sounds like the answer

parts.note: a dyer colours textiles

explanation.surface: A textile worker is said to be awful at the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means extremely bad or terrible.

clue.text: On reflection, son, 24, accepting booing ref regularly is appalling

indicators.note: reflection means mirroring, so the whole assembly is read backwards
accepting means taking in, so the regular letters go inside the other word

parts.note: 24 refers to the answer at 24 down, urge

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of booing ref is taken

explanation.surface: Booing the referee is shocking, a son reckons, after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes OIGE from 'booing ref'; 'accepting' puts it in URGE (24 down) to make UOIGERGE; 'On reflection' reverses S plus that.
explanation.definitionFit: Egregious means shockingly bad, outstanding in a negative way.

clue.text: Organ introduction dropped from musical

indicators.note: introduction dropped from means the first letter of the musical's title is removed

parts.note: Oliver! is the musical based on Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: An organ's introduction was cut from a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' reads as the instrument but means the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The liver is an internal organ of the body.
